title: performance-canary-enhanced-auto-detection-rollout-guards
author: Ava Chen
body: Summary: Improve the performance canary automatic-detection and rollout guard behavior by introducing an adaptive sensitivity detector with hysteresis, per-model latency/throughput baselines, and tighter integration with rollout policy enforcement. Motivation: We continue to see noisy false-positives in perf canaries during short transient spikes and KV-cache warmups. This PR reduces spurious rollbacks while preserving rapid detection of true regressions. Changes include: 1) Adaptive sensitivity detector: a new detector that adjusts detection thresholds based on recent baseline drift and sample variance, reducing sensitivity during startup/warmup windows. 2) Hysteresis + hold windows: configurable hysteresis and minimum evaluation windows to avoid flip-flopping with marginal metric changes. 3) Per-model baselines: ability to store and use model-specific latency/throughput baselines instead of global defaults. 4) Rollout guard integration: canary service now exposes guard decisions to the router; rollout policies can now opt into strict/lenient modes. 5) Tests & dashboards: end-to-end integration tests and updated canary dashboard/alerts for visibility. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2419) - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Backwards-compatible config defaults - [x] Rollout smoke test performed on staging - [x] Updated observability dashboards Migration notes: Config adds new fields (sensitivity_profile, hysteresis_ms, hold_window_seconds) with safe defaults that preserve previous behavior. Deployment: Feature guarded behind feature flag perf_canary_adaptive, default off in prod. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging and run canary tests (completed). 2) Enable feature for 10% of canaries with lenient mode for 48h and monitor. 3) If stable, increase to 50% and switch to standard mode. 4) Full rollout with strict mode after 3 days of stable metrics. Testing: - Unit tests for detector logic (edge cases, warmup) - Integration tests simulate latency/thru regressions and verify no false positive flips during warmup - Manual smoke: ran 50 simulated canaries in staging and validated zero false rollbacks for synthetic warmup spike. CI: All checks passed on final run. See CI summary below. Commits: See commits array field for per-commit summaries. Files changed: See changed_files field. Review notes: Addressed feedback about config naming (sensitivity_profile -> adaptive_profile) and added an explicit hold-window config to make intent clear. Also tightened logging around guard decisions for easier post-mortem. Release notes: Minor user-facing config additions for canary behavior; no breaking changes. Impact: Expected reduction in false-positive canary rollbacks, slightly slower reaction to single-sample spikes (intentional). Related PRs: refactors in perf-canary earlier this cycle (see ENG-2301).

test(canary): integration tests for warmup and transient spike scenarios
docs(canary): update canary runbook and dashboard links
chore(ci): add canary integration job to nightly pipeline
review_comments: Rashmi Patel: The hysteresis default looks sensible but can we add an explicit unit test for the edge where hold_window == 0?
Ava Chen: Added test 'test_zero_hold_window' in test_detector_integration.py and updated docs to call out behavior.
Ethan Liu: We should avoid reading baselines synchronously on every evaluation; can we cache for 30s?
Ava Chen: Implemented a 30s LRU cache in model-registry/store.go; added comment and test.
